title: UAE Investor Warns Indian Markets Face Correction as US Wobbles
excerpt: Jayesh Chandra Gupta, founder of UAEbased investment firm Peptomist, has warned that a correction in Indian equities may be imminent — triggered not by domestic fundamentals, but by the growing fragility of American m…
body:
Jayesh Chandra Gupta, founder of UAE-based investment firm Peptomist, has warned that a correction in Indian equities may be imminent — triggered not by domestic fundamentals, but by the growing fragility of American markets and the ripple effects of global uncertainty.

Gupta's argument centres on a familiar chain of causation for NRI investors: rising oil prices squeeze the rupee, a weak rupee pressures imported inflation, and the resulting tightening cycle chokes the equity rally. Add limited Indian exposure to the AI boom that has propped up US valuations, and Indian markets look vulnerable to a rerating if global liquidity dries up.

The warning comes at a sensitive moment. Asian markets fell sharply on May 14 amid fears of a potential Dubai debt crisis and a sliding dollar. Goldman Sachs and BlackRock have pegged US recession odds at 30–40 per cent by late 2026, while Moody's recently cut India's growth forecast to 6 per cent, citing elevated energy costs from the ongoing West Asia conflict.

For the Indian-American diaspora — many of whom hold dual portfolios spanning US and Indian equities — the message is one of caution. IT and pharma, the sectors most familiar to NRI investors, are among those Gupta flags as particularly exposed. Infrastructure and consumer plays, he suggests, offer better shelter.

The broader concern is liquidity. India's post-pandemic equity rally has been fuelled in part by global capital flows that could reverse quickly if the US Federal Reserve, now under new Chair Kevin Warsh, signals tighter-than-expected policy. Diaspora investors who piled into Indian markets during the 2023–25 bull run may want to reassess their hedging strategies.

A correction, if it comes, would not necessarily be catastrophic — Indian macro fundamentals remain resilient. But the era of easy gains appears to be drawing to a close.
author: Diaspora Desk
